issues.quote: `app.MapControllers()` itself runs once, at startup; it does not run again for every request
issues.text: Outline item 4 opens with "Program.cs runs top to bottom once, at startup". The lesson states run-once only for app.MapControllers(), never for the file as a whole; still established only by implication (carried over from r1, not applied).
issues.fix: In How it works, after "Its `Run()` call, at the very end, is what actually starts Kestrel." add: "Every line of Program.cs above `Run()` executes once, top to bottom, when the app starts." Covered by claims 2 and 5.

issues.quote: Only the order among `builder.Services.Add...` calls that register different things is free to vary.
issues.text: "Only" overstates: other Program.cs lines are also order-free with respect to request handling (e.g. the migration block at lines 57-62 could move among the Use* calls without changing how a request is answered). The lesson's own claim 3 supports only the Services.Add... half.
issues.fix: Replace with: "The order among `builder.Services.Add...` calls that register different things is free to vary; the order of the wiring calls is not."

issues.quote: The registration half of `Program.cs` — before `Build()` — only ever adds things the app might need:
issues.text: The first block ends at line 20 and the second starts at line 52 (`Build()`). Lines 21-51 are never shown or mentioned, so I cannot check 'only ever adds things' myself and do not know whether I am allowed to ignore them. The second block tells me exactly what to skip; the first does not.
issues.fix: Add one sentence after the first block saying what lines 21-51 hold (more registrations like these, belonging to later lessons) and that they can be skipped here.

issues.quote: It can matter when two calls register the same kind of thing, a case you do not need to look for in this lesson.
issues.text: I stop here: what counts as 'the same kind of thing'? Are OrderService and JwtTokenService different kinds because they are different classes, or because one is Scoped and one Singleton? The lesson tells me not to look for it, but quiz q6 option c reuses 'the same kind of thing' as if I knew.
issues.fix: Add a few words making 'kind' concrete, e.g. 'the same class (two registrations of `OrderService`)', or drop the sentence and reword q6 option c to avoid the phrase.

issues.quote: You notice this the first time a request behaves differently after a wiring line moves — which is what the next lesson is about.
issues.text: The misconception is believable, but the correction only asserts that wiring calls matter; I cannot picture one case in Đơn Hàng where moving a wiring line changes an answer. The only wiring call I understand is MapControllers.
issues.fix: Add one concrete clause using a line I already know, e.g. 'if `app.MapControllers();` were deleted, GET /api/v1/products would no longer reach `List()`'.

issues.quote: A connection string is registered earlier, but `Build()` itself does not open any connection; code that runs after it does.
issues.text: 'Code that runs after it does' points at the migration block the lesson told me to skip, so the explanation leans on something I was told not to read. I can still answer q1, but this line leaves me wondering which code opens the connection.
issues.fix: End the explanation at 'does not open any connection', or say 'code in a later lesson does'.

issues.quote: it should run before every request gets logged, not after
issues.text: The scenario is about `UseAuthentication` and `RequestLoggingMiddleware`, lines from the block I was told to skip. I can answer from the rule 'app.Use... between Build() and Run() is a wiring call', but I do not know what authentication does, so the reviewer's reason feels opaque.
issues.fix: In the context, add a short gloss: '`app.UseAuthentication()` (the wiring call that checks who the caller is)'.

issues.text: The stem is almost verbatim from the sentence after the second code block ('makes ... attribute-routed methods into real endpoints'), so I fill it by matching words, not by understanding.
